title: Po: half the transistors missing — NMOS-only bootstrapped sense amp
idea: Po: a sense amp without PMOS. Use an NMOS cross-coupled latch for sensing and restore the high side through a capacitive bootstrap that lifts an NMOS pull-up gate above VDD for a few ns, eliminating the n-well, PMOS implants and well-to-well spacing in the SA strip.
why: Periphery (#7) and capital (#4): SA strips lose ~30% width from well spacing and drop a couple of implant masks; Si, B, P, SiO2 only.

title: Si: laser-crystallized silicon pre-amp per bitline segment, excimer-free
idea: Deposit a-Si (SiH4 in H2) over the bitlines and crystallize it with a diode-pumped solid-state 532 nm laser instead of a XeCl excimer (xenon plus neon fill) to form a source-follower pre-amp on every 32-cell bitline segment, which then drives a long global bitline.
why: Hierarchical gain lets 4x longer bitlines share each SA stripe, cutting SA count ~4x (fact 7) and decoupling the needed Cs from bitline length (fact 1).

title: Bubble-memory boot loop replaces the fuse module entirely
idea: Bubble chips kept their own bad-loop map in an on-chip boot loop read at power-up. Store the redundancy map in the module's existing SPD EEPROM or the controller's NVM, and stream it into the die's repair latches during initialization over the mode-register interface. Laser and e-fuse blocks and their process steps go away, a net reduction in masks.
why: Removes fuse arrays and programming circuits (~2-4% of die, fact 7) and lets repairs be updated in the field.

title: JEDEC refresh-free mode with certified retention window
idea: Scale jump to the industry: a JEDEC mode-register bit disables refresh entirely and advertises a vendor-certified retention window (for example 2 s at 85 C) proven at qualification, and OSes and AI runtimes get a standard malloc_ttl API to place only data whose idle time fits.
why: Makes zero refresh deployable fleet-wide (fact 3) and lets vendors drop refresh logic from periphery (fact 7).

title: Canal locks with side basins: stepwise adiabatic bitline charging
idea: Water-saving canal locks fill and drain in steps from side basins and reuse most of the water. Raise the sense-amp rails (and so 8k bitlines) in 6-8 steps from on-die tank capacitors at intermediate voltages, and on precharge return each step's charge to its basin, so the supply only tops up resistive losses.
why: Bitline CV2 is the largest activation term (facts 8, 10); N-step charging cuts dissipation ~N, so 8 steps plus basin return of the discharging bitline gives ~6-10x; tank caps reuse DRAM's own capacitor process; ~2 ns extra latency.

title: Eliminate TSVs: infrared light links shining straight through thinned dies
idea: Silicon is transparent at 1.3 um, so bond InP micro-LEDs and place Ge photodiodes at the same x-y sites on every 30 um-thinned die, and each lane's beam passes vertically through a 12-high stack. Time slots or wavelengths pick which die speaks, so there are no TSV keep-out zones and no TSV yield loss.
why: Fact 6: attacks the TSV area tax and the 20-30% HBM yield loss and removes TSV etch and fill; target ~1 pJ/bit vertical links.

title: Printed thermistor film maps hotspots for per-bank refresh rates
idea: Worse: refresh every bank at the hottest corner's rate. Flip: laminate a printed thermistor array film (NTC oxide or carbon ink) over each die or under the lid, read by the controller to set each bank's refresh from its true local temperature.
why: Refresh (fact 3): retention roughly halves every ~10 C, so cool banks can refresh 2-4x less, cutting refresh energy ~20-40%.

title: Thousand-point on-die thermal map sets per-mat refresh
idea: MAGNIFY temperature sensing from 1-2 sensors per die to one ~50 um2 ring-oscillator thermometer per mat (~1,000 per die), and scale each mat's refresh interval to its local temperature, since leakage doubles roughly every 10 C.
why: Fact 3: in HBM stacks with 10-20 C gradients, refresh energy and bandwidth loss fall ~30-50%; area cost <0.1%.

title: Micro-bitlines with a gain transistor every sixteen cells
idea: Inverting 'cell charge must swing a long bitline by itself': bitlines are cut into 16-cell micro-bitlines (~3 fF) that each gate a single local gain transistor driving the global bitline, so a 1-2 fF capacitor gives a readable signal.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall: required Cs drops ~3x, so pillar aspect ratio can fall from ~70:1 to ~25:1, saving etch steps and yield.

title: Hot-mode dynamic twin-cell row pairing trades capacity for margin
idea: When a die or region runs hot, the controller pairs rows on complementary open bitlines into twin-cell mode (both wordlines fire, cells store opposite data), doubling differential signal and extending retention ~4-10x. Capacity halves only where and when needed.
why: Avoids designing all cells for worst-case 125 C retention (fact 1); refresh at hot drops sharply (fact 3).

title: CCD bucket-brigade shifts bitline charges to one shared correlated-double-sampling amplifier
idea: Effect: charge-coupled transfer. Turn local bitlines into buried-channel CCD registers: on activation, cell charges are clocked across 64 columns into a single low-noise floating-diffusion amplifier with correlated double sampling (scientific CCDs reach <5 e- noise), and written back by a reverse shift. One amplifier serves 64 bitlines and resolves ~100-electron packets.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and capacitor wall (fact 1): ~64x fewer sense amps and Cs up to ~20x smaller; the cost is ~32 ns of serial shift latency, which suits burst page fetches.

title: BEOL oxide-transistor preamps chop bitlines into tiny segments
idea: Ideal result: every cell has its own amplifier. Closest: one IGZO thin-film preamp in the BEOL above each 16-cell bitline segment converts the local charge into a current on a global bitline, so the silicon SA sees a large current signal instead of a millivolt swing.
why: Facts 1, 2, 7: local Cbl falls ~10x, enabling ~1 fF capacitors and 3D tiers whose short local bitlines need no per-tier silicon sense amp.

title: Printed trimmable reference ladder on package feeds bitline references
idea: Worse: replicate bandgaps, reference generators and trim fuses for VBLP, VREF and VPLATE on every die. Flip: print a ruthenium-oxide or carbon resistor ladder on the package substrate, laser- or inkjet-trimmed at final test, delivering filtered reference voltages to every die in the package.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): removes ~1-2% of die in analog reference circuitry and improves matching across a stack.

title: Core inhibit-wire counter-pulse cancels row-hammer disturbance
idea: Core memory's inhibit winding sent an opposing current to cancel unwanted switching. When a row activates, its two neighbor wordlines get a synchronized, shaped negative counter-pulse from the same sub-wordline driver, cross-wired in existing metal with no added mask. The pulse cancels the capacitive kick and electron-injection field that cause hammer flips.
why: Raises the row-hammer threshold from ~1k toward 10k+ activations (fact 9), shrinking or eliminating on-die TRR counter tables (fact 7).

title: Surface acoustic wave pulses select rows of magnetostrictive bits
idea: Inverting 'rows are selected by wires carrying current': a SAW transducer launches a strain pulse timed to reach the target row of magnetostrictive nanomagnets, lowering their barrier so a weak shared field line writes only that row, while reads use local MTJs.
why: Replaces high-current write drivers and per-row write selectors with timing; write energy ~10x lower; speculative.

title: NEMS relay power gates zero out idle subarray periphery leakage
idea: Reverse electronics to mechanics for slow switches: bank and subarray periphery power gates, toggled only on wake/sleep, are nanoelectromechanical relays from a U.S. MEMS foundry layer bonded above, giving true zero off-current.
why: Idle power: idle-bank periphery leakage (~20-30% of standby) -> ~0; ~1e9 lifetime switch cycles suffice for power gating.

title: Ormia coupled-ear switched-capacitor lever doubling bitline differential
idea: The fly Ormia ochracea links its eardrums with a lever that magnifies tiny interaural differences. Before latching, two small caps sample the bitline differential in parallel and are then switched into series, a charge-pump 'lever' that doubles delta-V while common mode stays put. The doubled signal goes to a standard latch.
why: Fact 1/7: a 2x larger delta-V relaxes Cs/Cbl by 2x, giving Cs ~2.5 fF or double-length bitlines with half the sense amps.

title: Vacuum-sealed cavities around bitlines minify parasitic capacitance
idea: MAGNIFY the air-spacer idea into a fully sealed vacuum tunnel: bitlines are suspended between storage-node contacts on periodic posts, a sacrificial carbon fill is ashed out, and a pinch-off dielectric seals the cavity, giving k~1 on three sides.
why: Fact 1: Cbl -45-50% versus nitride spacers, doubling signal so pillar height (and AR) can drop ~40%; also cuts bitline switching energy.

title: Few-electron planar cells with local two-transistor segment preamps
idea: Box: 0.3 fF planar MIM cap x IGZO access x local 2T gain preamp per 16 cells x monolithic BEOL x Si x no high-AR etch. Each cell stores ~1,800 electrons on a flat capacitor, a local preamp at each 16-cell segment amplifies it, and the ~1% errors from shot noise and leakage scatter are corrected by the code.
why: Capacitor charge wall: removes the 60-75:1 pillar entirely and can be stacked in BEOL tiers for 3D.

title: Servo-marked racetracks: hard-disk servo loop fixes domain-wall shift errors
idea: Failure mined: IBM's racetrack memory stalled on pinning-induced over- and under-shifting of domain walls. Fix: interleave a known servo pattern every 32 bits. The read MTJ's sense amp time-stamps each domain-wall arrival, and a per-track controller trims the next current pulse width, like hard-disk servo wedges.
why: Pushes shift error rates from ~1e-4 toward ~1e-12, so one read head can serve hundreds of bits and sense amps are shared over ~100x more bits (fact 7).

title: Switching-time sensing: read FeRAM by when the current peaks
idea: Constraint: non-volatile 1T1C ferroelectric cells shrunk until switching charge is tiny. Sense the time of the current spike rather than its charge: a peak detector plus time-to-digital converter on each bitline tells a switching cell (delayed nucleation peak) from a non-switching one (immediate displacement only), with no reference cell.
why: Immune to capacitor-area variation and fatigue-induced charge loss, so 3D FeRAM cells can shrink until switching charge is ~1 fC; no reference columns (periphery -5%).

title: 3D-NAND-like vertical CCD strings as capacitor-less DRAM
idea: Scale-and-time jump back to 1970s CCD memory, rebuilt as a 3D-NAND-style vertical string: each of 100+ stacked gate tiers holds a charge packet in an IGZO channel potential well, and a read clocks packets down the string (~10 ns per tier) into one floating-diffusion sense node at the bottom, then recirculates them to the top. No per-tier capacitor or lateral transistor exists; there is one sense amp per string.
why: Bypasses both 3D DRAM blockers, the capacitor and the lateral transistor (fact 2), and amortizes periphery over 100 tiers (fact 7); 5-10x the density of 6F2 if charge-transfer efficiency stays >0.9999, with wide-gap IGZO keeping dark current low.

title: Rubik's cube: re-keyed permutation shuffles physical row neighbors
idea: Twist the cube so neighbours change: put a 3-round keyed Feistel shuffle on the 6 low row-address bits in front of each mat's decoder and re-key it incrementally, swapping one row pair per refresh command, so logically adjacent rows map to unpredictable physical neighbours that keep moving.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): attackers cannot aim aggressors at a victim, removing most per-row counter area; cost is a few hundred gates per bank plus one row swap per refresh slot (~1% bandwidth).

title: Stepwise adiabatic charging of wordlines from on-die tank capacitors
idea: Limit: 4x less activation energy without lowering any voltage. Wordlines and bitline restore are charged in N steps from a bank of deep-trench tank capacitors held at intermediate voltages, then discharged back step by step into the same tanks, so dissipation scales ~1/N.
why: CV^2 floor (fact 10): with N=4, wordline and restore energy fall ~60-75% for ~1-2 ns of extra latency; the tanks reuse dead area under the pads.

title: Farmer's single tractor: one column decoder per bank group
idea: A farmer shares one tractor across fields that are never plowed at the same time. DDR5's tCCD_L already forbids back-to-back column commands within a bank group, so one column decoder and CSL driver set serves all four banks of the group through bank-select gating on shared column-select lines.
why: Cuts column decoder and CSL driver area ~4x (a few % of die, fact 7) with no change to timings or pins.

title: Kerf-line test periphery that dies at dicing
idea: Time-scale mismatch exploited: BIST engines, fuse programmers and test muxes are used for hours but occupy die area for years, so build them in the 60-80 um scribe streets, wired across a gapped seal ring at a low metal level, and let dicing destroy them (seal closed by post-dice passivation).
why: Recovers ~3-5% of die area spent on test/DFT periphery (fact 7), raising good die per wafer at near-zero cost.

title: Si: porous-silicon layer transfer reuses one seed wafer
idea: Grow periphery substrates as thin epitaxial Si (SiH2Cl2/H2) on an electrochemically porosified seed wafer (ELTRAN-style), split them off with a water jet and reuse the seed 10-20x, avoiding argon-purged Czochralski pulling and Spruce Pine quartz crucibles for most periphery wafers.
why: Cuts argon and high-purity quartz per periphery die ~90% and pairs naturally with bonded periphery; lowers wafer cost.

title: Taking out: periphery made in U.S. mature fabs, bonded to arrays
idea: TRIZ #2 Taking out pulls the ~49% periphery off the EUV array wafer: sense amps, decoders, pumps and I/O are made on 28-40 nm logic wafers in existing U.S. fabs and hybrid-bonded face-to-face at ~1 um pitch onto array-only wafers. A national 'periphery foundry' program qualifies one bonding interface that several array suppliers can use.
why: Facts 4 and 7 plus U.S. manufacturability: array die area per bit ~-45%, array wafer masks ~-20-30%, and about half of each DRAM's value-added silicon moves onshore without building an EUV fab.

title: Local wordline decoders with embedded antifuse tags for repair
idea: Give every local row decoder a tiny antifuse-programmed address-tag comparator, so any spare row in a mat answers for a failed address directly; the central fuse bank, fuse-broadcast bus and redundancy-compare stage are deleted, because the decoder and the repair CAM are now one cell.
why: Periphery (fact 7): repair logic and fuses are ~3-5% of die; also removes ~1 ns of compare from tRCD and allows finer, higher-yield repair.

title: Sense-amp latches become CPU-addressable cache, array the backing store
idea: Reverse the roles of periphery and array: SA latches become low-leakage retention latches that hold a row for milliseconds, tags live in the controller, and the open rows of all banks (tens of MB) serve as a directly addressed last-level cache; the array is touched only on misses.
why: Facts 5 and 8: 60-80% hit rates cut activations ~3-5x and access energy ~50%, and shrink the host's SRAM LLC.

title: Delay-line recirculating 3D string refreshes data by circulation
idea: As in mercury delay lines and drums, data in a vertical 3D DRAM string never sits still. The tiers are charge-coupled gates, and charge packets shift one tier per clock past a single regenerating sense amp at the string base, which restores each packet as it passes. No lateral access transistor is needed per tier, and refresh comes free with the circulation.
why: Attacks fact 2 (the lateral transistor blocks 3D) and fact 3 (refresh). One sense amp serves a 64-128-tier string. Random-access latency rises, so it fits capacity or streaming tiers.

title: All-zero row tags let periphery answer reads without activation
idea: Worse: sense and restore 8 KB of zeros exactly like useful data. Flip: keep a per-row pattern tag in a small SRAM in the bank periphery; rows tagged all-zero or repeated-pattern are answered by the column logic without activating the row and skipped by refresh until written.
why: Refresh and overfetch (facts 3, 8): zero or duplicate pages are often 10-30% of memory; their refresh and activation energy goes to ~0.

title: Sense amps chain into a shift register for streaming readout
idea: AI KV-caches read whole rows in order, so in streaming mode the SA latches daisy-chain into a shift register clocked out at the mat edge, bypassing column select lines and the column decoder; random access keeps only a coarse 8-way select.
why: Column decoder and CSL area (~5%) shrinks and fact 8's 128x overfetch becomes useful data; streaming energy per bit ~40% lower.

title: Remanent-polarization offset trim inside each sense latch
idea: Place a tiny AlScN or HZO ferroelectric capacitor (both <=400 C) on each SA latch node and partially polarize it at test so its remanent charge cancels that SA's offset, MINIFYING offset to near zero with no trim SRAM or DAC.
why: Fact 7: SA transistors can shrink ~4x; the trim is nonvolatile and can be re-set in the field as devices age.

title: Radio-frequency tone addressing selects wordline groups via resonators
idea: MINIFY decoder wiring to a single line: the row address is broadcast as a sum of on-die RF tones, and each wordline-driver group has a tuned LC or MEMS resonator filter bank that fires only when its tone combination is present.
why: Fact 7: replaces predecode buses and NAND decode trees (several % of die) with one global line; selectivity and latency make this speculative.

title: Goto-pair tunnel-diode latch as two-terminal sense amplifier
idea: Revive the 1959 Goto pair: two ALD MIM resonant-tunneling (negative-differential-resistance) diodes in series form a bistable node; the bitline nudges the midpoint and a clock pulse latches it, MINIFYING the SA to two diodes plus one access TFT, all <=300 C.
why: Fact 7: SA area -70-80% if a peak-to-valley ratio >3 can be reached in low-temperature MIM stacks; device physics is speculative.

title: Charge-domain popcount on sense stripes prefilters KV-cache tokens
idea: Store 64-bit locality-sensitive-hash signatures of keys; after sensing, each SA XNORs its bit with a broadcast query bit and dumps a unit charge onto a mat-level summing capacitor, whose voltage (Hamming similarity) one ADC per mat reads. Only top-scoring tokens' full keys leave the chip.
why: KV-cache data movement (fact 5) cut 5-20x for long contexts; analog in-place compute needs no advanced node.

title: Sense amps that self-trim offset over months via charge trapping
idea: Time jump from nanoseconds to months: each SA input transistor carries a nitride charge-trap spacer, and whenever on-die ECC corrects an error on that SA's column a micro-pulse traps a little charge to null the offset, so offsets anneal toward zero over field life and track aging.
why: Recovers the ~10-20 mV offset budget, raising sense margin ~20-30% so Cs or tRCD can shrink (facts 1, 7) and aging margin loss is cancelled.

title: Discarding and recovering: JEDEC managed-DRAM class without on-die repair
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: a new JEDEC 'managed DRAM' class removes laser/e-fuse repair banks, redundancy muxes and most wafer-sort retention testing from the die; the host discovers bad rows and columns at boot with a BIST march, discards them and recovers capacity from 5-10% over-provisioning, as NAND does with bad blocks.
why: 100x enabler: repair periphery (~5% of die) and test (~10-15% of cost) go away, and arrays can be built in low-cost, defect-tolerant processes that are unshippable today; trade-offs: capacity varies per part and boot-time mapping is required.

title: Controller-side remap tables replace on-die fuse redundancy
idea: Substitute on-die laser/e-fuse banks and redundancy address comparators with a per-device bad-row/bad-column table held by the memory controller (like an SSD FTL), filled at test and refreshed during field scrubbing.
why: Periphery area and yield: removes ~3-5% of die area for fuses and compare logic, and finer-grained repair raises yield on immature nodes.

title: Dead-zone sense amps flag uncertain bits as erasures, not errors
idea: Box: pillar cap x Si access x dual-offset comparator with dead zone x per-column flag bit x bulk Si x standard. Each SA has two skewed comparators; when they disagree the bit is marked erased, and since Reed-Solomon corrects twice as many erasures as unknown errors, a 1% raw BER that is mostly flagged costs only ~4-6% parity.
why: Absorbs 1% cell BER with less code overhead than blind ECC, so SAs and Cs can shrink.

title: Leakage-balanced bistable floating body that needs no refresh controller
idea: Inverting 'leakage is the enemy': floating-body cells are biased so gate-induced drain leakage generation and junction recombination balance at two stable body potentials, so each cell holds its state statically and the refresh counter, scheduler and temperature-based refresh logic are deleted.
why: Removes refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% idle power) and its 10-20% bandwidth tax plus refresh periphery; capacitor-free.

title: Twin-FeFET race: first-to-conduct wins, no reference needed
idea: Inverting 'sensing compares a cell against a reference': each bit is stored as opposite polarizations in two FeFETs; their shared gate is ramped and a tiny arbiter latches whichever drain current crosses first, so the decision needs no reference voltage and the read is nondestructive.
why: Eliminates reference generators and restore, rejects common-mode Vt drift and temperature, and drops read energy to the arbiter's few fJ; 2 cells/bit offset by vertical 4F^2 FeFETs.

title: Vt-tracking wordline high voltage relieves hot oxide stress
idea: Access Vt falls ~1 mV/K, so at 125 C the wordline needs ~100 mV less overdrive than at 25 C. Scale VPP down with temperature exactly by the Vt tempco, cutting oxide field when TDDB is most accelerated (~3x lifetime gain).
why: Enables thinner WL oxide and lower CV^2 energy at hot while meeting 10 y (fact 10).

title: Tungsten-free periphery: molybdenum contacts and plate-layer routing
idea: Limit: zero tungsten (China ~80% of supply). Replace W contacts and M0 in the periphery with ALD molybdenum or ruthenium, and reuse the capacitor top-plate film (TiN/doped SiGe) as an extra local routing layer for decoder and SA interconnect, deleting one W metal level.
why: Scarce-resource chokepoint and cost: removes W supply risk, saves one metal and mask level (~2-3% wafer cost), and Mo's lower resistance at small CDs speeds wordline straps.

title: Undersea-cable photonics replace global I/O lines via DUV photonic die
idea: Telecom crosses oceans with WDM light: a 45 nm DUV silicon-photonics die hybrid-bonded to the DRAM carries bank data on SiN waveguides, with microring modulators at each bank edge, replacing long global I/O metal lines and pin SERDES.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5) toward ~1 pJ/bit and global routing area freed, with no EUV.

title: Cuckoo strategy: host raises the on-die ECC and hammer logic
idea: Cuckoos let other birds raise their chicks. Write a JEDEC-style proposal plus open reference RTL in which the host controller does what each die's periphery does today (on-die ECC, refresh-management counters, thermal refresh) using metadata in ordinary rows, so 'lean' dies can omit those circuits. Three engineers, FPGA demo and standards work, ~$900k in 24 months.
why: Fact 7: on-die ECC alone adds ~6% array plus logic. Moving it and hammer counters to the host could reclaim ~6-10% die area per bit.

title: Nanoimprint-patterned pitch-matched sense and decoder strips
idea: Substitute immersion/EUV exposures of the highly repetitive pitch-matched sense-amp and subword-driver strips with UV nanoimprint from an e-beam-written master. University nanofabs routinely run NIL for such periodic patterns.
why: Capital (fact 4): imprint tools cost ~1/20 of a scanner per layer, and periodic periphery is ideal imprint content.

title: Registering clock driver stores weak-row map, targets refresh
idea: Load a per-row retention profile (from test or in-field scrubbing) into a small SRAM in the DIMM's registering clock driver, which is already a trailing-node chip; it lowers auto-refresh frequency and inserts targeted ACT/PRE refreshes only for the ~0.1% weak rows.
why: Refresh (fact 3): ~3-4x fewer refresh operations, reclaiming ~10% bandwidth and ~20% idle power on DDR5 modules without changing the DRAM die.

title: Bank-to-bank charge recycling during bitline precharge
idea: Worse: dump each bank's charged bitlines back to the VDD/2 rail and pay again to charge another bank. Flip: before equalizing, connect the high-side bitlines of a closing bank through a charge-transfer switch to the bitlines of the bank about to restore, so charge is reused instead of wasted.
why: Energy per bit (facts 8, 10): ~30-40% of bitline swing energy recovered on interleaved workloads.

title: Two bits per cell using old nodes' fat capacitors
idea: Trailing 2x-3x nm DRAM nodes have ~15-25 fF cells; pair that surplus charge with time-domain multilevel sensing, where a ramped reference and a counter in the SA stripe quantize four charge levels per cell.
why: Density and cost per bit (facts 1, 4): ~1.8x bits per wafer after ECC overhead, from fully depreciated old fabs with no new lithography.

title: Self-referenced double read only for test-flagged weak cells
idea: MRAM-style self-reference: read the cell, write a known '1', read again and compare both levels on the same SA input, cancelling per-cell Cs variation and SA offset. Applied only to the ~0.1% weak cells flagged at test via a small address table.
why: Lets the bulk population run with ~2x thinner margins (smaller Cs, longer refresh) while the tail is rescued (facts 1, 3).

title: Gap-junction wordline charge sharing between closing and opening rows
idea: Neurons joined by gap junctions pass charge directly. When one subarray's wordline (at VPP ~3 V) closes and another's opens, a pass switch first shorts the two, so about half the charge moves from the falling line to the rising one. The VPP pump then supplies only the remainder.
why: Fact 10: VPP comes from a ~30-40% efficient pump. Recycling ~50% of wordline charge cuts VPP energy ~40% and lets the pump, a large periphery block, shrink ~30%.

title: Cold-grade bin: immersion racks run retention-reject DRAM dies
idea: Effect: Arrhenius thermally activated junction leakage (~0.6 eV). A 10-person firm buys dies that fail the 85 C/64 ms retention test at scrap prices, has an OSAT package them, and deploys them only in single-phase immersion racks held at 30-40 C, where retention is ~8-16x longer and the dies pass with margin. An off-the-shelf FPGA/CXL controller checks retention at operating temperature.
why: Usable supply: reject bins (an estimated 2-5% of output) become sellable memory with zero fab capex.

title: Sell DRAM by the perishable byte-second
idea: Datacenter-scale business model: memory is priced per byte-second of guaranteed retention; 'perishable' refresh-free SKUs ship with no refresh engine and a certified 10 s window at a 30-40% discount, and tenants pay a premium only for data that must outlive it, served from NV tiers.
why: Zero refresh power across the perishable fleet (fact 3), smaller periphery and better binning yield; gives customers a reason to annotate data lifetimes.

title: Double-ended sub-wordline drivers survive any single driver failure
idea: Ideal result: a wordline that cannot be cut off. Drive each sub-wordline from both ends with drivers that can be disabled individually; if self-test finds one dead or a mid-line break, the other end drives the line.
why: Removes a top cause of row fuse-outs and halves wordline RC delay, enabling longer wordlines and fewer driver stripes (fact 7).

title: Photomultiplier dynode cascade pre-amplifier for femtofarad cells
idea: Borrow the photomultiplier's dynode chain: the bitline feeds a stack of three gated-diode charge amplifiers, each transferring and multiplying the packet (~3x per stage by collapsing a gate-boosted capacitance) before the latch fires. A 1.5 fF cell then looks like a ~20 fF cell to the latch.
why: Capacitor charge wall: Cs can drop from ~5 fF to ~1.5 fF, so pillar AR goes from ~70:1 to ~20:1, or 3D tiers can use small lateral caps. Costs ~5% SA area.

title: Time-domain sensing converts bitline signal into delay
idea: Ideal result: sensing that improves with digital scaling, not analog headroom. Each bitline drives a current-starved inverter whose delay depends on its voltage; a column-shared time-to-digital converter decides the bit and also reports margin or multi-level information in the same pass.
why: Voltage floor and periphery (facts 7, 10): time resolution improves each node while voltage headroom does not; works below 0.6 V supplies.

title: Shadow-evaporated single-electron transistor electrometers sense cryo-DRAM bits
idea: Substitute the CMOS sense amp with an Al/AlOx single-electron transistor (double-angle shadow evaporation, e-beam resist bridge) whose island couples to the bitline, reading sub-attofarad charge for 4 K memory beside quantum processors.
why: Charge wall: cell capacitance could shrink ~100x for cryogenic memory, making a planar cell possible with no high-AR capacitor.

title: Resonant LC tank recovers bitline swing energy adiabatically
idea: Pacemakers count every picojoule: bitline restore is driven by a sinusoidal resonant supply from an on-interposer inductor network, so bitlines charge adiabatically and return their energy to the tank at precharge instead of dumping it to ground.
why: Bitline charging dominates activation energy; 50-70% recovery would cut fact 10's stuck CV^2 per activation ~2x.

title: Successive-approximation sense amp magnifies bits per capacitor
idea: MAGNIFY bits per cell to two: after charge sharing, a 3-step successive-approximation sense amp with a capacitive DAC shared among 4 bitlines resolves four charge levels and writes back the quantized level during restore.
why: Facts 1 and 4: doubles bits per capacitor for ~1.3x SA area, a cost-per-bit gain worth ~2 nodes; risky because each level keeps only ~1/3 of the margin.

title: Po: no reference — read, write midlevel, read again
idea: Po: a sense amp with no reference. Charge-share the cell onto the bitline and hold the result on sample cap A, write VDD/2 into the cell, re-open the wordline and hold the second result on cap B, then compare A vs B; both samples traverse the identical path, so wordline kickback, bitline-pair imbalance and open-bitline layout mismatch cancel.
why: Capacitor wall (#1) and periphery (#7): removes ~10-20 mV of systematic offset, allowing ~30% lower Cs or 2x longer bitlines (half the SA strips); the extra latency suits a density-optimized capacity tier.

title: Ferroelectric-stored offset trim lets sense amps resolve 5 mV
idea: Ideal result: a sense amp with zero offset. At wafer test, each latch's mismatch is measured and written as a polarization state into a small FeFET in its tail or body-bias path, so the offset stays cancelled with no trim registers, fuses or periodic calibration.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): required bitline signal falls from ~20 mV to ~8 mV, allowing ~2x smaller Cs or 2x longer bitlines, cutting SA stripes (fact 7) by up to 40%.

title: Array-only fabs bond to US logic-foundry periphery wafers
idea: Split the business: a new entrant builds an array-only fab (capacitors and access devices, no periphery CMOS), and buys periphery wafers from US 22-28 nm logic foundries, joined by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding with periphery under the array.
why: Capital intensity and US manufacturability (fact 4): array fab capex and mask count drop, periphery uses existing US capacity; ~30-40% lower entry capex.

title: S: thiol monolayers self-align periphery contacts without lithography
idea: Use alkanethiol (C, H, S) self-assembled monolayers that bind only to exposed metal and block growth there, so dielectric grows only on dielectric in N2-purged area-selective ALD and vias self-align, removing via-litho layers and argon-sputtered liners.
why: Saves 2-3 masks per periphery stack (fact 4) and reduces contact-to-gate shorts so decoders pack tighter (fact 7), all without rare gases.

title: Zn+Sn+Cu: indium-free oxide CMOS tier for row decoders
idea: Build n-type amorphous zinc-tin oxide and p-type Cu2O thin-film transistors in BEOL above the mats to host row decoders and wordline drivers; the wide-bandgap channels block 3 V with sub-fA leakage, and using only Zn, Sn, Cu and O avoids the indium and gallium of IGZO.
why: Moves decoder and driver area (a major part of fact 7's 49%) on top of the array using abundant elements; ~10-15% die area recovered and driver leakage cut ~100x.

title: Core-memory sense weaving cancels sneak current in selectorless 3D crosspoint
idea: Failure mined: core memory's sense wire zig-zagged through the cores so half-select noise cancelled, a trick lost in the move to semiconductors, while selectorless vertical crosspoints died on sneak current. Fix: pair each data pillar with a woven twin pillar that crosses the same word planes, with its half-selected cells biased in mirror image. A differential sense amp subtracts the matched sneak currents and leaves only the selected cell's current.
why: 10x at the same cost: without a selector, 32 deposited word planes stack under one pillar etch (4F^2 per tier, roughly 1.5 tiers' worth of patterning cost), ~10-20x bits/mm^2. The twin pillar doubles pillar count, not cost.

title: Complementary oxide-TFT sense amplifiers built in the metal stack
idea: Box: 1T1C x IGZO access x CMOS-TFT latch (n-IGZO + p-SnO) x monolithic over array x Si x 400 C sputter BEOL. Cross-coupled latches and column muxes are made as stacked oxide thin-film transistors directly over the cell array, so periphery stops competing for silicon area.
why: Periphery ~49%: die area -30-40% at the same capacity using non-EUV, low-temperature tools; p-type oxide mobility is the risk.

title: Setun-style ternary global pre-decode cuts address wiring
idea: Soviet engineers built the ternary Setun computer when parts were scarce. Drive global pre-decode lines in balanced ternary (three-level signals with multi-Vt CMOS receivers), so 9 trits replace 14 bits and the pre-decode gate count drops.
why: Global address and pre-decode wiring shrinks ~35%, trimming the decoder share of periphery (fact 7).

title: Near-miss flagging sense amps drive traffic-based adaptive refresh
idea: Worse: refresh every row at worst-case 64 ms because nobody knows which cells are weak. Flip: add a cheap offset-biased secondary latch per sense-amp group that flags reads whose signal landed near the trip point during normal traffic; flagged rows enter a small refresh-priority table while all other rows run 4-8x longer refresh intervals.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3): retention-aware refresh with no offline profiling; ~50-70% refresh reduction at 32-64 Gb.

title: Coffee straw: partial-charge sip reads defer restore for many reads
idea: Sip through a straw instead of draining the cup: drive the wordline only into weak inversion for ~5 ns so ~10% of the cell's charge (~0.25 fC) flows into a clamped bitline and onto a 0.5 fF integrating sense node (~0.5 V signal); the cell stays readable and is restored only every ~5 sips or at refresh.
why: Removes per-read restore, full bitline swing and the 3 V wordline pulse: ~10x less energy per read for read-mostly data such as AI weights; risks are weak-inversion variability and tracking a sip count per row.

title: Po: bitlines live on the wafer's backside
idea: Po: a bitline on the other side of the wafer. After front-side capacitor and buried-wordline formation, bond to a carrier, thin to ~500 nm, and pattern bitlines and the SA strip on the backside, contacting access-transistor drains through nano-vias, so bitlines never run between capacitor pillars or beside wordlines.
why: Capacitor wall (#1) and periphery (#7): bitline capacitance drops ~40% (no BL-to-storage-node or BL-to-WL coupling), giving ~1.6x signal per fF of Cs, and SAs get a whole wafer face of area.

title: Repurpose OLED inkjet lines to print panel-level memory interposers
idea: Worse: build all new memory packaging capacity from scratch. Flip: convert idle Gen-6/8 OLED inkjet-printing and TFT lines into panel-level printers of interposers, decap sheets and periphery TFT layers for memory packages.
why: Capital and time: tools already exist, cutting packaging capacity lead time from years to months.

title: Merchant periphery wafers: U.S. array startups build only arrays
idea: Reverse vertical integration: one U.S. fab sells known-good periphery wafers with a standard hybrid-bond map, while startups and national labs fabricate only array wafers (~20 fewer masks) in small U.S. fabs and bond them domestically.
why: Capital intensity: an array-only line could cost ~1/3 of a full DRAM fab, multiplying U.S. supply sources.

title: Lego standard: open array-to-periphery hybrid-bond interface
idea: A child snaps any brick onto any brick. Publish an open, royalty-free standard for the bonded interface between DRAM array wafers and CMOS periphery wafers (pad pitch, bitline mux ratio, sense-node electrical spec, test hooks) so array makers and logic fabs can mix and match.
why: Lets U.S. logic fabs supply periphery wafers and new array startups skip the 49% periphery design burden, lowering capital and entry barriers (facts 4, 7).

title: Royalty-free JEDEC array-to-periphery bonding standard
idea: Failures mined: RDRAM died in a royalty war and Gen-Z in consortium fragmentation. Fix: a JEDEC standard for the hybrid-bond interface between DRAM array wafers and periphery wafers (bond map, preamp electricals, test hooks), backed by a royalty-free patent pool. Any U.S. logic fab can then sell periphery wafers to any array maker.
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: periphery (~49% of the die) moves to commodity logic fabs, cutting the capital needed to enter DRAM by ~30-40%.

title: Paraffin latent-heat buffer keeps DIMMs below the 2x refresh threshold
idea: Effect: latent heat and melt/freeze thermal hysteresis. Bond an encapsulated paraffin/graphite phase-change pad (melting ~75-80 C, ~200 J/g) between DRAM packages and the heat spreader; during load spikes it clamps die temperature below 85 C so the controller never enters JEDEC 2x refresh, and it re-solidifies in lulls.
why: Refresh bandwidth/energy (fact 3): ~10-20% bandwidth recovered on hot servers; off-the-shelf materials and a small hardware team.

title: Bitline as LC resonator read by frequency-division multiplexing
idea: Make each segmented bitline part of an LC tank (top-metal spiral over the array plus bitline capacitance) with its own resonant frequency; the cell charge shifts a varactor-loaded resonance, and one wideband RF receiver per mat reads 16 bitlines at once by FDM, replacing 16 pitch-matched latch sense amps. This combines RF filter-bank receivers with DRAM sensing.
why: Periphery ~49% (fact 7): one shared receiver per 16 bitlines; ~20-30% die-area savings if inductors fold over the array.

title: Microwatt refresh island: coin cell keeps IGZO memory alive for years
idea: Constraint: data survives mains loss, with no NV material. Pair hour-retention IGZO DRAM with a tiny always-on periphery island (a ~2 uW clock, counter and row walker) that refreshes one row every ~1 ms from a 20 mAh lithium cell or harvested trickle, while all other periphery is cut off.
why: Quasi-NV with full DRAM endurance and speed; a 32 Gb die needs only ~0.4 uW of refresh, so the cell lasts ~2 years without ferroelectric wear or backup dumps.

title: Trusted-foundry legacy fabs supply U.S. DRAM periphery dies
idea: Defense programs already fund trusted 90-45 nm U.S. fabs; a policy program pays these lines to make DRAM periphery and base dies (SAs, decoders, I/O) for hybrid bonding to array wafers, backed by offtake guarantees from federal and hyperscaler buyers.
why: U.S. manufacturability: roughly half of DRAM die function made domestically with no EUV, using existing capex.

title: Half-full bucket: restore depth set by refresh pointer position
idea: A child carries a half-full bucket when the next stop is close. The die knows where its internal refresh pointer is, so after an access it restores a row only to ~85% charge when that row's refresh is imminent and fully when it is far away.
why: Cuts restore and SA drive energy ~20-30% per activate (facts 8, 10) while tRAS on the bus stays the same.

title: Open university interposer testbed decouples arrays from sensing logic
idea: Substitute captive DRAM-fab periphery development with an open platform: a university-built passive Si interposer with 2 um microbumps joins test cell arrays (MIM caps plus IGZO access devices) to FPGA or shuttle-ASIC sense logic, so any lab can iterate on sensing schemes in weeks.
why: US manufacturability and innovation speed: lowers the cost of experimenting with new sensing physics from fab-scale to ~$100k, broadening the US talent and IP base.

title: NbN nanocryotron sense amplifiers with superconducting niobium bitlines
idea: Substitute both the copper bitline and the CMOS latch with superconductors: zero-resistance Nb bitlines feed an e-beam-patterned NbN nanocryotron (nTron) whose choke switches the channel normal when the bitline current exceeds its threshold.
why: Energy per bit: superconducting sensing costs aJ per event and has no bitline RC, enabling multi-thousand-cell bitlines and ~10x fewer sense amps for cryogenic computing.

title: Deposition-defined vertical decoder transistors replace lithographic gate lengths
idea: Like MEMS and solar fabs that set critical dimensions by film thickness, decoder transistors are vertical channels whose gate length is an ALD film thickness and whose width is a spacer thickness; logic personalization is done with implants at relaxed DUV pitch.
why: 10 nm-class decoder devices with no EUV, keeping decoder area competitive (facts 4, 7).

title: Flying-spot optical wordline addressing replaces drivers and pumps
idea: Modernize the Williams-tube flying-spot scanner. A backside micro-LED or waveguide-grating array lights one row of photogated access-transistor gate lines, and a stacked photovoltaic diode string on each subarray gate line supplies the gate overdrive, replacing the VPP pump. The CMOS row decoder becomes a light-source driver on a separate cheap die.
why: Removes row decoders, sub-wordline drivers and VPP charge pumps (a large part of the 49% periphery, fact 7) and takes the 3 V wordline off the logic node (fact 10).

title: Roll-to-roll imprinted fan-out film replaces silicon interposer for HBM
idea: Worse: wire HBM to the GPU on large, expensive silicon interposers limited by reticle stitching. Flip: produce 2 um line/space redistribution films by roll-to-roll UV imprint and plating on polyimide, laminated as an organic interposer carrying the memory PHY lanes.
why: Capital intensity and HBM cost: interposer cost per mm^2 drops ~5-10x and size is no longer reticle-limited.

title: Fe: electroplated permalloy domain-wall counters track row activations
idea: Electroplate Ni-Fe nanowire loops (no argon PVD) as magnetic domain-wall counters, as in multi-turn rotation sensors, per row group; each ACT current pulse advances a wall one notch by spin-transfer, and an anisotropic-magnetoresistance stripe flags when a threshold notch is reached.
why: Nonvolatile, leak-free row-hammer counters (fact 9) without SRAM tables, ~0.1 um2 each in BEOL.

title: Vacuum canning: no-air-break integration of periphery gate and contacts
idea: Canned food needs no preservatives because it never meets air. Run the periphery gate stack (interface, high-k, metal, cap) and the contact module (etch, liner, fill) each in one vacuum cluster with in-situ dry cleans, so wafers never grow native oxide or pick up airborne contamination, and queue-time wet re-cleans disappear.
why: Water: ~10-15 inter-step wet cleans per periphery flow are removed (~10x less water in those modules), along with queue-time scrap; cycle time also falls.

title: Shift-token wordlines replace decoders for streaming AI weights
idea: Ideal result: no address decoding because the next row is always known. For weight-streaming tiers, chain sub-wordline drivers into a shift register so a single token ripples row to row; only stream entry points use a coarse decoder.
why: Periphery area (fact 7): row decoders shrink ~80% in streaming mats; inference reads weights sequentially, so random row access is rarely needed.

title: Single-transistor-type periphery built from the array's own vertical channels
idea: Ideal result: periphery that costs zero extra masks. Design sense amps, drivers and decoders entirely from the array's vertical-channel access transistor, with a few gate lengths set by etch depth, dropping the separate high-k metal-gate planar CMOS flow for core periphery.
why: Capital and masks (fact 4): removes ~10-15 periphery mask steps and 1-2 EUV layers; periphery and array share one process.

title: Chef's early taste: column read from half-resolved sense amps
idea: A chef tastes before the dish is done. A small comparator on the local I/O pair reads the SA nodes once they split by ~150 mV and sends data down the column path while the main latch keeps restoring cells; a late-flip detector cancels the burst in the rare disagreement.
why: Trims ~3-5 ns (~25%) off tRCD and lets SA transistors be weaker and smaller because restore leaves the critical path (fact 7).

title: MicroLED mass transfer of GaN-HEMT periphery chiplets onto glass
idea: Borrowed from microLED mass transfer: GaN HEMT sense-amp and driver chiplets (~50 um) are grown on sapphire, laser-lifted off and stamped thousands per second onto IGZO cell arrays on glass, then wired with panel metal.
why: Fast (2DEG mobility ~1500 cm2/Vs), high-voltage periphery with no silicon wafer, EUV or quartz crucible anywhere in the flow.

title: Po: dies talk without touching — inductive-coupled stack I/O
idea: Po: a memory stack with no data TSVs. Replace HBM data TSVs with vertically aligned on-die Cu/Al spiral coil pairs (inductive coupling through thinned dies), keeping only a few large power TSVs for supply.
why: HBM TSV tax (#6): removes most TSV keep-out area and the 20-30% TSV yield loss; coils use standard metal, no W fill or Ta liners.

title: Chopped dither comparator reads signals below its own offset
idea: Reverse noise's role: a tiny comparator fires 16 times in ~2 ns with a known dither added and its inputs swapped every other decision; an up/down counter shared per 8 bitlines cancels the offset (it flips sign with the chop) while the dither linearizes, recovering the sign of a signal far smaller than the offset.
why: Facts 7 and 1: comparators ~0.3x today's SA area still resolve ~10 mV, enabling ~2 fF cells; energy of 16 micro-decisions is below one full latch swing on a long bitline.

title: Vanadium-dioxide hysteretic latch held inside its Mott window
idea: Inverting 'volatile memory must leak and be refreshed': each cell is a tiny VO2 element biased inside its metal-insulator hysteresis window, so it stays metallic or insulating as long as the hold bias is on, and a current comparator reads the ~100x resistance ratio.
why: One-element static cell with no refresh controller, no capacitor and a large read signal; hold power and thermal crosstalk are the risks.

title: Splat-quenched metallic-glass gates kill grain-driven sense-amp mismatch
idea: Borrow rapid-quench casting of metallic glass: deposit the SA gate metal as an amorphous alloy (e.g., Ta-Si-N or Zr-Cu-Al sputtered on a cold substrate) with no grains. With no random TiN grain orientations there is no grain work-function variation between the two latch transistors.
why: Work-function variation is a leading Vt-mismatch source in high-k metal-gate periphery; removing it cuts SA offset sigma ~30-40%, so bitline signal (and Cs or VARY) can drop ~25-35%.
